posts.title: The M-Vave FM-1 FM Synthesizer And The Success Of Open Source
posts.description: The M-Vave FM-1 Synthesizer is a small synthesizer with silicone keys and a small 2.7cm colour display. It is designed around reproducing the sound of the Yamaha DX7, which is a synthesizer that was used in a lot of popular music throughout the 80s. With 27 keys in a standard layout the device can be played like any (very small) piano. The device has built in MIDI and Bluetooth MIDI so it can be easily connected to any keyboard to extend it's capabilities. The default operating system that comes with the FM-1 has an arpeggiator and sequencer that give users the ability to create their own compositions and play back their creations. At only 16.1cm wide and 9.6cm deep the FM-1 is just slightly bigger than a phone and has a built in battery, meaning that you can pop it in a pocket and create compositions on the go. At just £50-60 the FM-1 is also amazing value, which means that it is much more affordable than most synthesizers on the market. It also comes in a variety of different colours

posts.title: Drupal Paradigms
posts.description: Drupal Paradigms I've been using Drupal for a number of years now, and I've built up a set of paradigms (or heuristics) that help me with building Drupal sites. These are based around both using Drupal as well as developing and maintaining Drupal sites, and even web development in general. When putting together content types or building Drupal modules I have these rules at the back of my mind, guiding my actions. They've even been used in more than one sales document where I talk about how we work. In this article I will look into a set of Drupal paradigms, with some explanation about each one. I'll also add example where possible to illustrate my thoughts. First, let's start with a classic. posts.title: Xteink X4 Pocket Reader: A Review
posts.description: I've been happy with my Kobo Aura ebook reader since I bought it 8 years ago. It's light, has a crystal clear e-ink display, a decent back light, and the battery still lasts quite a long a while. I've read many books on it, most of which I have bought through the Kobo store. The DRM free service they provide is very convenient and give me access to a wide selection of books for a reasonable price. When I go travelling I never take the Kobo Aura with me as it's a bit of an awkward size. It's larger than a phone and smaller than a tablet so it could easily fit into luggage, but it just never occurs to me to take it with me. I normally read ebooks on my phone via the Kobo app. I wasn't in the market for a new ebook reader at all, but when I saw the Xteink X4 pocket reader I was intrigued enough to look into it.
